newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds took a breather on Wednesday ahead of a spate of economic indicators due out on Thursday, but the rand wavered at weaker levels amid importer dollar demand.
At 1400 GMT the rand was at 4.4360/90 after opening at 4.4260/4210 on the dollar, compared to Tuesday's 4.4170/00 close.
Dealers said importer demand from the corporate side was strong during the morning session with some speculators moving in during the afternoon.
The weakness was attributed in part to the January trade data being delayed until Thursday, with investors viewing the postponement as negative.

"It can take away any confidence. You can't see missing trade figures positively," one dealer said. Another said rumours were circulating that the trade figures would be worse than expected, hence the deferral.
The currency appeared capped around 4.43 on the day although speculative dollar demand, which dealers said seemed to be aimed at triggering stop losses, pushed it weaker towards the close.
"We've seen importer demand at the 4.4230 level all the way up and a little speculating. It looks like a couple of guys want to take it up further probably because of stop losses," one dealer said.
Against the crosses the rand was last quoted at 7.2565/2659 against sterling from 7.2233/2326 on Tuesday and at 0.3780/3784 from 0.3789/3793 marks previously.
Bonds were moribund throughout the day. The key R150 was last at 14.52 percent, scarcely up from the 14.495 morning's opening and compared to Tuesday's 14.485 percent yield.
Traders said the bond market was extremely quiet with only small amounts of offshore institutional selling seen early in the day.
"It's been a very dull, boring day -- not much doing. The market probably needs to catch its breath and consolidation is what we've seen today. It's waiting for fresh news," one said.
The narrow range was adhered to after good strength over the last few days, and traders said the market was still in a bullish mode.
"The trend is still intact and its down," one trader said.
Traders said Wednesday's slowdown was due in part to the wait for trade, inflation, fourth quarter GDP, money supply and credit extension data, all due on Thursday.
On the money market, rates held steady between 16.50 and 16.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unmoved at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the daily shortage at 10.139 million rand on Tuesday from 10.178 billion rand on Monday.
Bond Exchange statistics show foreigners bought a net 245.80 million rand worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after selling 52.03 million on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 7.3 billion rand from 3.58 billion on Monday.
